title: Scope agent prompts to role-relevant context only
summary: Architecture analysis for replacing the one-size-fits-all pipeline.prompt embedding with role-appropriate context in agent prompts. Currently every agent (tester, documenter, integrator, etc.) receives the full issue body verbatim, and Tier 3 phase-scoped coders receive the entire plan draft including other phases. The recommended approach introduces a _build_role_context() helper and a _summarize_issue() helper to provide each role with focused context while keeping full information accessible on demand via file paths and CLI commands.

problem_statement.description: Every agent in the SDLC pipeline receives the full original issue body (pipeline.prompt) as 'Task Description', regardless of role. A tester gets the entire feature request narrative when it only needs to know what code changed and what to verify. A documenter gets technical constraints when it only needs to know what was built. In Tier 3 dispatch, the phase-scoped coder prompt embeds the entire plan draft even though the agent only implements one phase. This wastes context tokens and risks agents working outside their assigned scope.
goals: Replace full issue body with 1-2 sentence background summary for scoped roles (tester, documenter, integrator)
Include 'For more context' pointers in every scoped prompt (gh issue view, cat .egg-state/drafts/...)
Provide tester prompts with task descriptions, acceptance criteria, and files_affected instead of raw issue body
Provide documenter prompts with implementation summary instead of raw issue body
Filter Tier 3 phase-scoped coder plan embedding to overview + current phase detail only
Provide integrator prompts with structured summary of all phases instead of raw issue body
Keep full issue body for architect/task_planner/risk_analyst (they need it for analysis)
Update existing prompt tests to reflect new context structure

_build_agent_prompt.mechanism: Main dispatcher for role-specific prompts. Delegates CODER/REFINER to _build_phase_prompt(), REVIEWER_* to _build_review_prompt(). For all other roles (tester, documenter, integrator, architect, task_planner, risk_analyst), builds a shared context header, embeds pipeline.prompt verbatim under '## Task Description' (lines 2014-2018), then appends role-specific instructions.
_build_agent_prompt.key_issue: The 'if prompt:' block at lines 2014-2018 unconditionally embeds the full issue body for ALL non-coder, non-reviewer roles. No role-based filtering of context content exists.

_build_phase_scoped_prompt.mechanism: Builds Tier 3 coder prompts scoped to a single plan phase. Reads the full plan draft via _read_phase_draft() and embeds it in a markdown code block (lines 2293-2304). Then renders phase-specific task checklist (lines 2306-2320). Does NOT embed pipeline.prompt directly.
_build_phase_scoped_prompt.key_issue: The plan embedding at lines 2302-2304 includes the ENTIRE plan draft. Other phases' detailed task lists, acceptance criteria, and file lists are included even though the coder should only see its own phase's details. The phase scope section (lines 2307-2320) correctly limits the task checklist, but the plan section above leaks all phases.

_run_tier3_implement.mechanism: Orchestrates Tier 3 phase-level dispatch. For each plan phase, runs coder -> tester -> documenter -> checker -> reviewer. After all phases, runs integrator.
_run_tier3_implement.tester_prompt_construction: Lines 2555-2579: Calls _build_agent_prompt(prompt=pipeline.prompt, ...) which embeds full issue body, then appends phase scope lines with task list and files_affected.
_run_tier3_implement.documenter_prompt_construction: Lines 2631-2642: Calls _build_agent_prompt(prompt=pipeline.prompt, ...) — gets full issue body with no additional phase scoping appended.
_run_tier3_implement.integrator_prompt_construction: Lines 2961-2990: Calls _build_agent_prompt(prompt=pipeline.prompt, ...) then appends Tier 3-specific integration instructions with phase list.

_run_multi_agent_phase.mechanism: Standard (non-Tier 3) multi-agent execution. Loops over get_roles_for_phase() and calls _build_agent_prompt(prompt=pipeline.prompt, ...) for each role. Same issue — all roles get the full prompt.
_run_multi_agent_phase.key_code: Lines 3106-3121: Iterates roles, calls _build_agent_prompt() with pipeline.prompt for every role.

handoff_data_flow.mechanism: Handoff data flows via EGG_HANDOFF_DATA environment variable (set in multi_agent.py:160-169), NOT via prompts. Agents parse it at runtime. Contains changed_files, commits, and other outputs from upstream agents.
handoff_data_flow.formatter: orchestrator/handoffs.py:281-314 — format_handoff_for_prompt() exists but is not currently used to embed handoff data in prompts.
handoff_data_flow.note: The handoff mechanism is out of scope for this issue — it works correctly.

classes_tested: TestBuildCheckerPrompt — checker prompt modes (discovery vs explicit)
TestBuildPhasePromptPlanEmbedding — plan/analysis embedding in implement phase
TestReadSharedCriteria — shared file loading with user overrides
TestSharedPromptFileContent — shared criteria file content verification
test_coverage.gap: No tests exist for _build_agent_prompt() role-specific context. No tests for _build_phase_scoped_prompt() plan filtering. No tests for Tier 3 tester/documenter prompt content.

implementation_approaches.name: _build_role_context() helper (recommended)
implementation_approaches.description: Create a new _build_role_context(role, pipeline, phase_obj=None) function that returns role-appropriate context markdown. Create a companion _summarize_issue(title, body) function that extracts a 1-2 sentence summary. Replace the 'if prompt:' block in _build_agent_prompt() with a call to _build_role_context(). For _build_phase_scoped_prompt(), add plan filtering logic to show overview + current phase detail + one-line summaries of other phases.
pros: Single point of control for role-context mapping — easy to extend for new roles
Matches the design proposed in the issue
Clean separation: _build_role_context() handles what context; _build_agent_prompt() handles prompt structure
Helper can be unit tested in isolation
Manageable diff size — modifies 3-4 functions, adds 2 helpers
cons: Requires parsing/summarizing the issue body, which may be fragile if formats vary
Introduces a new abstraction in already-complex prompt building code

implementation_approaches.name: Inline role-specific branches (no helper extraction)
implementation_approaches.description: Expand the existing role-specific if/elif block in _build_agent_prompt() to include role-specific context before '## Your Task'. Move the 'if prompt:' block inside the conditional, so architect/task_planner/risk_analyst get the full body while scoped roles get inline summaries.
pros: Minimal structural change — no new functions
Easier initial review since changes are localized
cons: _build_agent_prompt() is already 300 lines — adding context per role makes it harder to maintain
Plan filtering for Tier 3 would duplicate logic
Harder to test individual role context in isolation
Does not match the issue's proposed design

implementation_approaches.name: Per-role prompt builder functions
implementation_approaches.description: Create separate _build_tester_prompt(), _build_documenter_prompt(), _build_integrator_prompt() functions. Have _build_agent_prompt() dispatch to these.
pros: Maximum clarity — each role's prompt is fully self-contained
cons: Significant duplication of shared prompt structure (header, restrictions, completion)
Divergence risk — shared improvements must be applied to every builder

recommended_approach.name: _build_role_context() helper
justification: The refine analysis already recommended this approach, and it aligns with the issue's proposed design
Provides clean separation of concerns: context selection vs prompt structure
The _build_role_context() helper is independently testable, making it easy to verify each role gets the right context
The _summarize_issue() helper is simple — issue title + first paragraph truncated at ~200 chars. The issue states 'A few hundred extra tokens of useful background is fine'
Manageable scope: core changes in one file (pipelines.py), new tests in one file (test_pipeline_prompts.py)

_summarize_issue.signature: _summarize_issue(title: str | None, body: str | None) -> str
_summarize_issue.behavior: Returns a 1-2 sentence summary. Uses issue title as the first sentence. Extracts the first paragraph of the body (up to ~200 chars, truncated at sentence boundary). Returns empty string if both inputs are None.
_summarize_issue.location: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (new, near other helpers around line 1090)
_summarize_issue.test_strategy: Unit test with various issue bodies: short, long, markdown-heavy, empty

_build_role_context.signature: _build_role_context(role: str, pipeline: Pipeline, phase_obj=None, handoff_summary: str | None = None) -> str
_build_role_context.behavior: Returns role-appropriate context markdown for embedding in the prompt. Dispatch by role: (1) architect/task_planner/risk_analyst → returns pipeline.prompt verbatim (full issue body), (2) tester → returns summary + task descriptions with acceptance criteria + files_affected + 'For more context' pointers, (3) documenter → returns summary + implementation summary from handoff + files changed + 'For more context' pointers, (4) integrator → returns summary + structured phase summary + test results from handoff + 'For more context' pointers, (5) all others → returns summary + 'For more context' pointers.
_build_role_context.location: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (new, near other helpers around line 1090)
_build_role_context.test_strategy: Unit test each role path: verify contains expected sections, omits full issue body for scoped roles, includes full body for analysis roles

_build_agent_prompt.change: Replace lines 2014-2018 ('if prompt:' block) with a call to _build_role_context(role_value, pipeline_obj, phase_obj). The function needs to accept either a Pipeline object or the prompt string — recommend adding an optional pipeline parameter alongside the existing prompt parameter for backward compatibility, or extracting the issue title from the prompt (first line). For architect/task_planner/risk_analyst, _build_role_context returns the full prompt. For scoped roles, it returns the focused summary.
_build_agent_prompt.backward_compatibility: All call sites already pass pipeline.prompt as the 'prompt' parameter. The _build_role_context() function needs access to the Pipeline object for the issue title and phase data. Two options: (a) pass the Pipeline object as a new parameter, or (b) pass issue_number and title separately. Option (a) is cleaner since the Pipeline is available at all call sites.
_build_agent_prompt.impact: All non-coder, non-reviewer roles will see different prompt content

_build_phase_scoped_prompt.change: Replace lines 2293-2304 (full plan embedding) with filtered plan content: (1) Extract the plan's overview/summary section (everything before '## Implementation Phases' or the first '### Phase'), (2) Embed the current phase's detail in full, (3) Show other phases as one-line summaries: 'Phase N: [name] — [goal]', (4) Add pointer: 'For full plan: cat .egg-state/drafts/...'
_build_phase_scoped_prompt.plan_parsing: The plan follows a template (docs/templates/plan.md) with '## Summary', '### Phase N: [Name]' sections, and '## Test Strategy'. Parse by heading level: H2 for top-level sections, H3 for phases. Extract current phase by matching phase_obj.id or phase_obj.name. This parsing is simple string splitting — no markdown parser needed.
_build_phase_scoped_prompt.impact: Tier 3 coders will see a more focused plan prompt

_run_tier3_implement_tester.change: Instead of calling _build_agent_prompt(prompt=pipeline.prompt, ...) then appending phase scope lines, call _build_agent_prompt() with role-context that already includes the phase scope. The _build_role_context('tester', ...) function will include task descriptions, acceptance criteria, files_affected from phase_obj when provided. The separate phase_scope_lines appended at 2567-2579 can be simplified or removed since the role context already contains this information.
_run_tier3_implement_tester.alternative: Keep the existing append pattern but have _build_agent_prompt use _build_role_context for the base context. The phase scope lines at 2567-2579 provide additional Tier 3 focusing — these can remain as-is since they augment rather than duplicate.
_run_tier3_implement_tester.impact: Tier 3 testers will see focused context instead of full issue body

_run_tier3_implement_documenter.change: Same pattern as tester — _build_role_context will provide focused context instead of full issue body.
_run_tier3_implement_documenter.impact: Tier 3 documenters will see focused context instead of full issue body

_run_tier3_implement_integrator.change: _build_role_context('integrator', ...) will provide a structured summary of all phases. The Tier 3-specific integration instructions appended at 2974-2990 can remain as-is.
_run_tier3_implement_integrator.impact: Integrator sees structured overview instead of full issue body

_run_multi_agent_phase.change: Need to pass Pipeline object (or issue title + phase context) to _build_agent_prompt() so _build_role_context() can construct appropriate context. Currently only passes pipeline.prompt as the 'prompt' parameter.
_run_multi_agent_phase.impact: Standard multi-agent execution will use role-scoped context

parameter_threading.problem: _build_agent_prompt() currently receives 'prompt: str' (the raw issue body). To build role-specific context, _build_role_context() needs: (1) the Pipeline object or issue title, (2) optionally a phase_obj for Tier 3 scoping, (3) optionally handoff_summary for downstream roles.
parameter_threading.recommended_solution: Add optional parameters to _build_agent_prompt(): 'pipeline: Pipeline | None = None' and 'phase_obj: Phase | None = None'. When pipeline is provided, use _build_role_context() for context building. When only prompt is provided (backward compatibility), fall back to the existing behavior. All 4 call sites (_run_tier3_implement tester/documenter/integrator, _run_multi_agent_phase) have the pipeline object available, so threading it through is straightforward.
parameter_threading.alternative: Add 'issue_title: str | None = None' parameter instead of the full Pipeline object. This is more minimal but less flexible for future context needs.

constraints: Architect/task_planner/risk_analyst must continue to receive the full issue body — they need it for analysis
Reviewer prompts (_build_review_prompt) are out of scope — they have their own prompt construction
Handoff data mechanism (EGG_HANDOFF_DATA env var) is out of scope — no changes to how handoff data flows
Refiner role delegates to _build_phase_prompt(), not _build_agent_prompt() — no changes needed for refiner
Coder role delegates to _build_phase_prompt() for standard dispatch — no changes needed for standard coders
Every agent prompt must include a 'For more context' section with pointers to full context
Summary should be 1-2 sentences, not nothing — agents need orientation for good judgment calls
Plan filtering should preserve the overview/summary section — coders need to understand how their phase fits
Existing test patterns use string presence/absence assertions — new tests should follow the same pattern
The _build_agent_prompt function signature change must not break _run_multi_agent_phase or _run_tier3_implement call sites

Contract Phase model (shared/egg_contracts/models.py) — provides phase_obj with tasks, acceptance criteria, files_affected
Plan template format (docs/templates/plan.md) — heading structure for plan parsing
_read_phase_draft() helper (pipelines.py:1065-1087) — reads plan draft from disk
_render_contract_tasks() helper (pipelines.py:1090-1133) — renders contract tasks as markdown

risk_assessment.mitigation: Use a simple approach: issue title + first paragraph. If parsing fails or body is empty, fall back to just the title. No complex markdown parsing needed.

risk_assessment.risk: Plan heading structure varies between drafts, breaking plan filtering
risk_assessment.mitigation: Plan template is standardized (docs/templates/plan.md). Use heading-level parsing (## for sections, ### for phases). If parsing fails, fall back to embedding the full plan with a warning comment.

risk_assessment.risk: Agent behavior regression — scoped agents lack sufficient context and spin
risk_assessment.mitigation: Every scoped prompt includes 'For more context' pointers with CLI commands (gh issue view, cat drafts). Agents can self-serve additional context. The summary provides orientation for judgment calls.

risk_assessment.risk: Test maintenance burden — new tests for each role's context
risk_assessment.mitigation: Follow existing test patterns (string presence/absence). _build_role_context() is a pure function — easy to test with mock Pipeline objects.

phase_outline.name: Core helper functions and _build_agent_prompt refactor
phase_outline.description: Implement _summarize_issue() and _build_role_context() helpers. Refactor _build_agent_prompt() to use _build_role_context() instead of embedding pipeline.prompt for scoped roles. Update _run_tier3_implement() and _run_multi_agent_phase() call sites to thread Pipeline object. Add unit tests for new helpers and modified function behavior.

phase_outline.name: Phase-scoped plan filtering and integration tests
phase_outline.description: Implement plan filtering in _build_phase_scoped_prompt() to show overview + current phase detail + one-line summaries of other phases. Add tests for plan filtering with various plan formats. Verify end-to-end behavior with existing test infrastructure.
